name: HiPixel
soft_passes: #2 optically centred but the split is asymmetric — divider sits left of centre, 'after' half takes the larger right two-thirds
#5 bezel is consistently top-lit with a matching baked shadow, but the interior bitmap has its own unrelated photographic lighting
#7 both halves are blue — figure-ground separation leans on texture (blocks vs brushwork) and the loud yellow divider, not tonal contrast
#8 sensible 2-plane frame->image stack, but the baked drop shadow z-fights the system-applied shadow
#9 Big Sur front-facing-squircle intent executed with flat-transition-era baked-shadow and non-full-bleed floating-frame habits
failures: #1 mask: floating white rounded-rect with a baked drop shadow on transparent canvas (corners alpha 0, artwork only ~80% of canvas) — reads as a sticker under the squircle mask and doubles the system shadow
#3 silhouette: filled solid it is an anonymous rounded rectangle; all meaning lives in interior texture
#4 16px squint: pixel grid, thin divider and Starry Night brushwork all smear into a blue/yellow blur at Dock/Spotlight size
#10 variant robustness: photographic/painterly interior cannot survive dark/clear/tinted/mono renders; a mono tint collapses the before/after into one tone

palette.background: no field — floating glossy white/silver bezel #E8EAED->#DDE0EF on transparent canvas with baked drop shadow

light_model: top-down: specular sheen on the bezel's top edge + baked soft drop shadow beneath (consistent); interior is a self-lit photographic/painterly bitmap with no modelled form light
layer_stack: before/after bitmap (blue pixel-grid left | Starry Night right)
devices: diagonal comparison-slider divider in shouting yellow
Van Gogh Starry Night as the demo subject
rhymes_hint: sample-image-in-a-glossy-white-frame image-utility icons; before/after split-screen comparison-tool icons (retouch/restore/diff-slider family)
notes: 512px web render, not the 1024 master — fine detail already softened, treat detail-loss reading with that caveat. Core structural finding: the icon is NOT a full-bleed squircle — it is a floating white rounded-rect frame (~80% of canvas, corners alpha 0) with a BAKED drop shadow, which fights the system mask and doubles the system shadow. Interior is a photographic/painterly bitmap, so it fails 16px, silhouette, and all tinted/dark/mono variants. Its one genuine strength is the literal before/after comparison device (subject-mined Starry Night). Strong palette coherence with the cover: the icon is a faithful miniature of the cover hero (same Starry Night before/after concept, same blue+yellow), so brand and icon read as one system. Photography category, image-upscaler subject — good candidate to seed a 'demonstrate-the-function-inside-a-frame' icon cluster if 2+ more image tools rhyme.
